Subject: Venue retainer and cost-center coding for Chicago field studio

Hi team —

Quick one: Eventique (vendor) just sent a standard venue retainer to hold our field studio in Chicago for Sept 28–29. Quote attached — $12,000 retainer to secure venue and basic AV (see Eventique_Retainer_Quote.pdf attached).

We need two things confirmed by EOD Wed 8/4 so we can lock the date:
- Finance coding: which cost center / GL should this hit? Project tag will be RW-FIELD-2027-08.
- Procurement path: can we charge the retainer on a p-card (single trans cap) or do we require a PO? If PO, can procurement issue a short-form PO before EOD?

Attachments included: SOW_FieldStudio_Chicago.pdf, cost_breakdown.xlsx, Eventique_Retainer_Quote.pdf

Notes:
- Retainer is refundable only up to 30 days out; venue will not hold without deposit.
- Total event budget estimate (venue + catering + speaker fees + misc) ~ $29k. Retainer is $12k of that.

Asking for an expedited lane here — this is a customer-facing event and the space is limited. If anyone needs more info from the vendor, Kate at Eventique (kate@eventique.com) is on this thread.

Thanks,
Connor

Connor — thanks for the heads up.

Quick answers:
- I can route this to procurement, but Finance needs to confirm GL/cost center first. Tagging Ben for confirmation.
- P-card single-transaction cap for events is $5,000. Anything above requires a PO or procurement-approved exception. Splitting across two p-cards to work around the cap triggers additional review and is frowned upon.

If we need a PO, procurement can do a short-form PO if Ben confirms the GL and we provide vendor EIN/W-9 and remit address. Marissa — can you send vendor details and the preferred remit info so I can open a ticket?

-Stephanie

Connor / team —

Finance can route this to GL 5400-FIELD. Please include project tag RW-FIELD-2027-08 on all docs; that will make month-end chargeback easy.

A few specifics:
- P-card single-transaction limit = $5,000. We cannot approve a single-card charge for $12k.
- Procurement should issue a short-form PO for the $12k retainer (PO ceiling = $20k for short-form). Procurement can expedite and route to me for priority review.
- Required vendor docs before PO issuance: W-9 / tax ID, remit address, and a contact for invoice submission.
- Contractor/third-party reimbursement: capped at $150/day unless pre-approved; receipts required.

I can provisionally approve issuance of a PO once procurement has the vendor W-9 and quote. I attached a template for the short-form PO (PO_template_shortform.pdf) and our contractor expense policy (contractor-expense-policy.pdf).

Ben Carter
Finance Manager | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Connor —

Responding to your two points:
- Splitting across two p-cards still looks like an attempt to circumvent single-transaction controls and will trigger an audit flag; not recommended.
- For the local producer (contractor): set them up as a T&E reimbursement or vendor payment depending on whether they can provide an invoice + W-9. If they can invoice, add them as a vendor and issue payment via PO / AP — cleaner for bookkeeping. If reimbursement via p-card is required, receipts and the $150/day policy apply; anything over that needs pre-approval by Finance.

I have provisionally created a short-form PO number to hold the retainer while procurement finalizes vendor setup: PO-47721-P (provisional). Procurement should convert this to a full PO when vendor setup completes.

Ben
